title: Must & Have to — scopri la regola
topicTag: Must · mustn't · have to · don't have to

questions.text:
🔍 **Leggi la scena.** Non c'è nessuna regola: scoprila tu!

❓ Nelle frasi con **have to / has to**, chi decide che cosa bisogna fare?
options: Altre persone: la mamma, la scuola, le regole
questions.ttsText: Mum: Tom, get up! You have to catch the bus at seven thirty! Tom: Oh no… and I have to do my maths homework! Lisa: Ha ha! And Tom has to walk the dog, Mum! Mum: Yes, he has to. And you have to help me, Lisa! Mr Brown: School rules. Students have to wear a uniform.

questions.text:
🔍 **Guarda di nuovo la scena.** Quando si dice **have to** e quando **has to**?
Trascina ogni soggetto nella colonna giusta.
questions.ttsText: Mum: Tom, get up! You have to catch the bus at seven thirty! Tom: Oh no… and I have to do my maths homework! Lisa: Ha ha! And Tom has to walk the dog, Mum! Mum: Yes, he has to. And you have to help me, Lisa! Mr Brown: School rules. Students have to wear a uniform.

questions.text:
✍️ **Ora scrivi tu la regola!** Clicca le parole giuste.
Con **I / you / we / they** si usa [[have to|has to]].
Con **he / she / it** (Tom, Lisa…) si usa [[have to|has to]].
Dopo have to il verbo è [[base (catch)|con -ing (catching)|con -s (catches)]].
Have to vuol dire: devo, perché [[lo vuole qualcun altro|lo voglio io]].

👀 **Avevi ragione?** Controlla la regola qui sopra.

❓ **Which is correct?**
options: She has to tidy her room.
She have to tidy her room.
She has to tidies her room.

questions.text:
Complete with **have to** or **has to**.
The boys [[have to|has to]] study hard.
My sister [[have to|has to]] wake up at 7 o'clock.
We [[have to|has to]] wear a uniform at school.
My dog [[have to|has to]] stay in the garden.

✍️ **E tu? What do you have to do at home?** Write 2 or 3 sentences.
*Example: I have to make my bed. My brother has to walk the dog.*
🙋 **Hai capito l'uso di HAVE TO?**
options: ✅ Sì prof, tutto chiaro! — It's all clear!
🤔 Ho qualche dubbio — I've got some doubts
❌ Non ci ho capito niente — I didn't get a thing!

questions.text:
🔍 **È sabato!** Leggi i messaggi di Tom e Lisa.

❓ "I **don't have to** get up early" vuol dire…
options: Non è necessario che mi alzi presto
questions.ttsText: Tom: It's Saturday! I don't have to get up early. We don't have to go to school today! Lisa: And I doesn't… oops! I don't have to do my homework. Tom: Mum doesn't have to work. She can sleep! Mum: Yes… but Tom, you have to tidy your room!

questions.text:
🔍 Lisa si corregge: dice "I **doesn't**… oops! I **don't** have to".

❓ Perché? Guarda anche la frase sulla mamma.
options: Con I si usa don't; doesn't si usa con he / she / it (Mum)
Doesn't è sbagliato in tutte le frasi
Con I si usa doesn't, con Mum si usa don't
questions.ttsText: Tom: It's Saturday! I don't have to get up early. We don't have to go to school today! Lisa: And I doesn't… oops! I don't have to do my homework. Tom: Mum doesn't have to work. She can sleep! Mum: Yes… but Tom, you have to tidy your room!

questions.text:
✍️ **Scrivi tu la regola!**
I / you / we / they → [[don't|doesn't]] have to
he / she / it → [[don't|doesn't]] have to
Dopo doesn't si dice [[have to|has to]]: Mum doesn't ___ work.

👀 **Avevi ragione?** Controlla la regola qui sopra, poi completa.
We [[don't|doesn't]] have to get up early on Sundays.
He [[don't|doesn't]] have to get up early on Sundays.
My parents [[don't|doesn't]] have to work today.
Luca [[don't|doesn't]] have to do the washing-up: it's my turn!

🔍 **Sam fa delle domande a Tom.** Guarda come iniziano le domande e come risponde Tom.
Per fare la domanda metto all'inizio [[Do / Does|Have / Has]].
Con Lisa (she) uso [[Does|Do]].
Tom risponde "Yes, I [[do|have]]" e "No, she [[doesn't|hasn't]]".
questions.ttsText: Sam: Do you have to wear a uniform at your school? Tom: Yes, I do. A blue jumper and grey trousers! Sam: Does Lisa have to wear a uniform too? Tom: No, she doesn't. She's at a different school.

questions.text:
👀 **Avevi ragione?** Controlla la regola.

❓ **Does he have to eat the vegetables?** ✅
🔀 Put the words in order to make a **question**.
sentences: Does she have to play today?

questions.text: 🔀 Put the words in order to make a **negative** sentence.
🔗 Match the parts of the sentence: *They don't have to come here.*

🔍 **Leggi i post-it, i messaggi e i cartelli.**

❓ "I **must** call Grandma": chi ha deciso che Tom deve chiamare la nonna?
questions.ttsText: Tom: I must call Grandma, it's her birthday! Sam, this film is amazing, you must watch it! I must study more. I want a good mark! Lisa: Look at the signs at the pool. You mustn't run. You mustn't eat here. Mrs Green: Shh! In the library, students mustn't shout.

questions.text: ❓ E nei cartelli: "You **mustn't** run" vuol dire…
questions.ttsText: Tom: I must call Grandma, it's her birthday! Sam, this film is amazing, you must watch it! I must study more. I want a good mark! Lisa: Look at the signs at the pool. You mustn't run. You mustn't eat here. Mrs Green: Shh! In the library, students mustn't shout.

questions.text:
✍️ **Scrivi tu la regola!** Guarda: I must… you must… students mustn't…
Con he / she si dice: She [[must|musts]] call Grandma.
Dopo must il verbo è: She must [[call|to call|calls]].
Mustn't vuol dire: [[è vietato|non è necessario]].

👀 **Avevi ragione?** Controlla la regola.

❓ Your bike is broken and you want to ride it tomorrow. **Which is correct?**
options: I must to fix my bike.

questions.text:
🚫 Look at the sign and complete.
**You mustn't ___ here.**

🚫 Look at the sign and complete.
**You mustn't ___ your phone in class.**

🚫 Look at the sign and complete.
**You mustn't ___ in the library.**
🏫 **School rules!** Must or mustn't? Drag each rule into the right column.

✍️ **Your class rules!** Write 3 rules for your class: what you **must** and **mustn't** do.
*Example: We mustn't use our phones in class. We must help our classmates.*
🔍 **Due frasi negative… stesso significato?** Leggi la scena, poi metti ogni frase nella colonna giusta.
items: You mustn't drive on the pavement.
You mustn't use your phone in the exam.
You don't have to get up early on Sunday.
You don't have to drive – we can get a train.
You don't have to wear a uniform today.
questions.ttsText: Lisa: Look at this sign at the pool. You mustn't dive here. Danger! Mum: It's Sunday. You don't have to get up early. Sleep! Dad: Remember, you mustn't drive on the pavement. Mum: And you don't have to drive, we can get a train.

questions.text:
👀 **Avevi ragione?** Controlla la regola, poi scegli.
You [[mustn't|don't have to]] drive on the pavement. It's against the law.
You [[mustn't|don't have to]] drive – we can get a train.
It's a holiday: we [[mustn't|don't have to]] wear our uniform.
You [[mustn't|don't have to]] touch the paintings in the museum.
❓ In Britain cars drive on the left: it's the law. **Which sentence is right?**
options: In Britain you have to drive on the left.
In Britain you don't have to drive on the left.
In Britain you mustn't drive on the left.
